transcript.text: dyson keeps pulsin on n off like its stutterin, wont stay on proper. batt is full. pls help

This sort of pulsing is usually the Dyson protecting itself because airflow is restricted — most often a blockage or a clogged/damp filter. It is not usually a sign that the battery is flat, even if it is fully charged. 1. Switch it off and unplug it, or remove the battery if it comes out. Empty the bin, then look through the wand, floorhead and bin inlet for compacted fluff, hair or an object. A clear airway should let light through. Clear anything you can safely reach. 2. Check the filter. If it is dirty, wash it in cold water only, then leave it to dry fully for at least 24 hours before refitting. Even slightly damp filters can cause pulsing. 3. Turn the floorhead over and remove hair/thread from the roller. It should turn freely by hand; a jammed roller can also make it cut in and out. If it runs steadily with the wand or floorhead removed, the restriction is in the removed section. If it still pulses after the airways are clear and the filter is clean and completely dry, the remaining possibilities are battery protection/a tired battery or an internal motor/electronics fault, which is better assessed by a Dyson repair service.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — A vacuum that pulses or cuts out after running is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage starving the airflow — check and clear those before suspecting battery, charger or motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

its a v8 animal. emptied the bin, cut some hair off the brush bar and pulled a big clump of hair n cat litter out the bottom of the wand. filter has never been washed, its grey not purple lol, will wash it now. no burning smell, no heat, battery not swollen

The large hair/litter blockage plus a filter that has never been washed make restricted airflow by far the most likely cause. The pulsing is normally protection doing its job, rather than the battery failing. 1. Do not use detergent or heat. Leave it somewhere warm and airy for at least 24 hours, then refit it only when it is completely dry — a damp filter can itself make it pulse. 2. Before refitting, with the battery removed, check the bin inlet and the short airway where the wand joins the machine for any remaining compacted litter or fluff. The brush bar should turn freely after the hair removal. Anything left there can cause the same pulsing. Then try it on normal power. If it now runs steadily, it was the blockage/filter and no part is indicated. If it still pulses with the filter fully dry and all airways clear, try it briefly with the wand and floorhead removed: steady without them points to a remaining restriction in the wand/head; still pulsing bare points more towards the battery or an internal motor/electronics issue, for which a Dyson repair service is the sensible next step.
washed it, water came out black, left it overnight on radiator side. pulses way less but still a bit. also the wand clump is out, its fine now, proper suction no pulsin with the dry filter

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. That has fixed it — the pulsing was airflow protection caused by the hair/cat-litter blockage and dirty filter, not a battery fault. For prevention, empty the bin before it gets packed tight, check the wand/brush bar for hair occasionally, and wash the filter in cold water when it starts looking dirty. Let it dry completely for at least 24 hours before refitting; avoid putting it directly on a hot radiator. No part is indicated while it has proper suction and runs without pulsing.
